item.title: OSPFv2-Concept
item.description:
a large area dynamic routing protocol. Elect a Designated Router (DR) Elect Backup Designated Router (BDR) All other routers are Drothers highest score wins order of importance Interface Priority Router ID Loopback address Active IP address on any interface on the router NOTE: Interface Priority We don’t change the interface priority very often. the DR is responsible for collecting and distributing all of the Link State Advertisements (LSAs) within the area. it stores these in a database which it then is responsible for sending to all of the Drothers. the DR uses the multicast address 224.0.0.5 for all OSPF routers. the BDR maintains a close relationship with the DR and keeps a backup of all relationships and the database. in the event that the DR is no longer active it assumes the role of DR. its a read only version of the Link State Database all routers or layer 3 switches in an area that are neither a DR or a BDR. use the multicast address 224.0.0.6 to send messages to the DR and BDR also see WCM - Wild Card Mask

1 #> param( [ValidateSet("BIOS", "OS", "Service", "LogicalDisk")] [string] $InfoClass = "BIOS", [string] $Device = "LocalHost", [parameter(Mandatory = $false)] [string] $OutFile_Path ) #sets the variable for the type of data being collected if ($InfoClass -eq "BIOS") { $InfoClass_var = "Win32_Bios" } elseif ($InfoClass -eq "OS"){ $InfoClass_var = "Win32_OperatingSystem" } elseif ($InfoClass -eq "Service"){ $InfoClass_var = "Win32_Service" } elseif ($InfoClass -eq "LogicalDisk"){ $InfoClass_var = "Win32_LogicalDisk" } #creates the formatting for the teble and data if ($InfoClass -eq "BIOS"){ $Table_Data = Select-Object -Property SMBIOSBIOSVersion,Name,Version,SerialNumber,Manufacturer } elseif ($InfoClass -eq "OS"){ $Table_Data = Select-Object -Property SystemDirectory,Organization,BuildNumber,SerialNumber,Version } elseif ($InfoClass -eq "Service"){ $Table_Data = Select-Object -Property Name,ProccessID,StartMode,State } elseif ($InfoClass -eq "LogicalDisk"){ $Table_Data = Select-Object -Property DeviceID,@{name='FreeSpace';expression={[Math]::Round($_.FreeSpace / 1MB, 3)}}, @{name='Size';expression={[math]::Round($_.Size / 1GB, 3)}}, @{name='%Free';expression={[Math]::Round($_.FreeSpace / $_.Size * 100, 3)}} } #collects info $Device_Data = Get-WmiObject -Class $InfoClass_var -ComputerName $Device |Select-Object $Table_Data #creates file name and full path $File_Name = "$($Device)-$($InfoClass)-$(Get-Date -Format yyyy-mm-dd).csv" $OutFile_Path_compleate = $OutFile_Path + "\" + $File_Name #creates file if specifyed if ($OutFile_Path) { Get-WmiObject -Class $InfoClass_var -ComputerName $Device |Select-Object $Table_Data |Export-Csv -Path $OutFile_Path_compleate } #prints data to the terminal $Device_Data |Format-Table -AutoSize -Wrap

item.description: #Get-ServiceHealthReport.ps1 #Author: Ryder Fryling #Created: 2026/03/22 #Version 1.0 #Updated: N/A #Description: This script Audits Windows services by status, startup type, and service account. <# .SYNOPSIS Audits Windows services by status, startup type, and service account. .DESCRIPTION Queries Windows services using Get-Service and Get-CimInstance, then filters and reports based on the specified criteria. Useful for identifying stopped auto-start services, services running under non-standard accounts, or summarizing overall service health. .PARAMETER Status Filter services by status. Valid values: Running, Stopped, All. Defaults to All. .PARAMETER StartupType Filter by startup type. Valid values: Automatic, Manual, Disabled, All. Defaults to All. .PARAMETER AccountFilter If specified, shows only services running under this account name (partial match). For example, "LocalSystem" or "Network". .PARAMETER SortBy Property to sort results by. Valid values: Name, Status, StartType. Defaults to Name. .EXAMPLE .\Get-ServiceHealthReport.ps1 Lists all services sorted by name. .EXAMPLE .\Get-ServiceHealthReport.ps1 -Status Stopped -StartupType Automatic Shows only stopped services that are configured to start automatically (potential problems that need attention). .EXAMPLE .\Get-ServiceHealthReport.ps1 -AccountFilter "LocalSystem" -SortBy Status Shows services running as LocalSystem, sorted by their current status. #> param( [validateSet("Running", "Stopped", "All")] [string]$Status = "All", [validateSet("Automatic", "Manual", "Disabled", "Auto", "All")] [string]$StartupType = "All", [Parameter(Mandatory = $False)] [string]$AccountFilter, [validateSet("Name", "Status", "StartType", "StartMode", "State")] [string]$SortBy = "Name" ) #gets the services $services = Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_Service #sorts them by status if ($Status -ne "All") { $services = $services | Where-Object { $_.State -eq $Status } } #sorts them by start type if ($StartupType -ne "All") { $services = $services | Where-Object { $_.StartMode -eq $StartupType } } #filters the accounts to best match user input if ($AccountFilter) { $services = $services | Where-Object { $_.StartName -like "*$AccountFilter*" } } #formats the $SortBy to be valid input options if ($SortBy -eq "Status") { $SortBy = "State" } elseif ($SortBy -eq "StartType") { $SortBy = "StartMode" } #sorts the data then makes the table and formats it $services | Sort-Object -Property $SortBy | ForEach-Object { [PSCustomObject]@{ Name = $_.Name DisplayName = $_.DisplayName Status = $_.State StartType = $_.StartMode Account = $_.StartName } } | Format-Table -Property Name,Status,StartType,Account,DisplayName -AutoSize -Wrap

item.description: # date created: 05/03/2026 # date modified: 16/03/2026 # author: Erik Bjerstedt # # Synopsis: automatically creates AD users on the system from a CSV file # # Warning: This script assumes that your OU structure and naming (including capitalization) is identical to the project's ADDS diagram. # Before running, verify that your OUs are structured correctly. # # Citations: # ICT 128 Lab 07 - Full lab.pdf - Phase 3 used as reference # defining default password $defaultPass = ConvertTo-SecureString "S@lta5002!" -AsPlainText -Force # importing the csv $userList = Import-Csv -Path (Read-Host "Enter your CSV file's full path") Write-Host "$($userList.Count) users loaded from CSV." # processing CSV users foreach ($user in $userList) { # getting name $fName = $user.'First Name'.Trim() $lName = $user.'Last Name'.Trim() $fullName = "$fName.$lName" # building SAM and UPN $sam = ($fullName -replace '[^a-zA-Z0-9]', '').ToLower() $upn = "$sam@atlas.com" # building path $subDept = $user.Subdepartment $title = $user.Title if ($subDept.Length -gt 5) {$subDept = $subDept.Substring(0, 5)} forEach ($OU in (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -like "*"})) { if ($title.Contains("Owner")) { $OUPath = (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -eq "Owners"}).DistinguishedName break } elseif ($title.Contains("VP")) { $OUPath = (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -eq "VPs"}).DistinguishedName break } elseif ($title.Contains("Operations")) { $OUPath = (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -like "Operations*"}).DistinguishedName break } elseif ($title -ceq "CIO") { $OUPath = (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -eq "C-Suite"}).DistinguishedName break } elseif ($subDept -eq "Accou") { $OUPath = (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -eq "Finance"}).DistinguishedName break } elseif ($SubDept -eq ("Administration")) { $OUPath = (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -eq "Administration"}).DistinguishedName break } elseif ($title.Contains("Administrator")) { $OUPath = (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -like "IT-Admin*"}).DistinguishedName break } elseif ($title.Contains("Technician")) { $OUPath = (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter {Name -eq "IT-Staff"}).DistinguishedName break } elseif ($OU.Name.Contains($subDept)) { $OUPath = $OU.DistinguishedName break } } # creating ADuser New-ADUser ` -GivenName $fName ` -Surname $lName ` -Name $fullName ` -DisplayName "$fName $lName" ` -SamAccountName $sam ` -UserPrincipalName $upn ` -Department $user.Department ` -Title $user.Title ` -AccountPassword $defaultPass ` -EmployeeID $user.'Employee ID' ` -Office $user.'Office Location' ` -OfficePhone $user.'Office Local Phone' ` -EmailAddress $upn ` -ChangePasswordAtLogon $true ` -Enabled $true ` -Path "$OUPath" # confirming creation $created = Get-ADUser -Identity $sam -Properties Enabled -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue if ($created){ # if user creation succeeds Write-Host "$sam successfully created (Enabled: $($created.Enabled))" -ForegroundColor Green Write-Host " SubDepartment: $($subDept), OU: $($OUPath)" } else { # if user creation fails Write-Host "Failed: $sam" -ForegroundColor Red } #reseting path $OUPath = "" } # finish message Write-Host "`nImport complete. $($userList.Count) users processed."

item.title: CIM vs WMI vs Native PS CMDlets
item.description: It is a Windows service that exposes hardware, operating system components, and software as structured objects that PowerShell (and other tools) can query. WMI has been built into Windows since Windows 2000. WMI is the windows version of CMI. it is no longer being developed or supported it is being phased out and is not in PS 7 It is a vendor-neutral standard published by the Distributed Management Task Force (DMTF) that defines how system components should be described as objects. WMI is Microsoft's Windows-specific implementation of this standard. the universal version of WMI used to get info about the OS is not available on windows 7 or older you will need to use WMI on those OS's cannot be piped ( | ) Namespaces are the top-level containers. They group related classes together. The most important namespace for network and system administration is root\CIMV2. PowerShell uses this namespace by default when you run Get-CimInstance without specifying one.Other namespaces serve specialised purposes: root\SecurityCenter2: antivirus and firewall product information root\WMI: hardware performance data root\MicrosoftDNS: DNS server management (on DNS servers only) My summery This is like the Directory/folder that the data is located in. Classes define the structure of a type of system component. A class lists all the properties that objects of that type have, along with their data types. Class names follow a convention: Win32_*: provided by the Win32 provider; covers OS, hardware, and networking CIM_*: base classes from the CIM standard; Win32 classes inherit from these __* (double underscore): WMI system classes, metadata about WMI itself My Summery this is the type/format of where the data comes from Instances are the actual data objects, one instance per real component matching the class template. The class Win32_NetworkAdapter defines what properties a network adapter object has; each installed adapter (physical and virtual) is a separate instance of that class.Note Some classes always return exactly one instance (Win32_OperatingSystem) there is only one operating system. Others return many (Win32_NetworkAdapter) one per adapter. Knowing which to expect is part of reading query output correctly.

Hyper-V and Hypervisors
item.description:
. A Hypervisor is the software layer on a physical host that coordinates virtual machines. A Hypervisor manages virtual machines and is responsible for allocating resources to each virtual machine. The Hypervisor is ultimately what makes virtualization possible. There are two types of Hypervisor: Type 1 and Type 2 Also known as the "Bare Metal Hypervisor" Type 1 Hypervisor is installed directly on the physical host Has direct access to the physical resources of the physical host which then allocates the available resources to the virtual machines Hypervisor loads (boots) first, before the Operating System Administrators have the ability to create clusters with many Type 1 Hypervisors (but not all) Also known as "Hosted Hypervisor" Type 2 Hypervisor is installed on top of the host Operating System (ie Windows 10) The host Operating System manages the hardware resources The Type 2 Hypervisor requests the resources from the Operating System Type 2 Hypervisors do not support clustering Type 1 Hypervisors have better performance compared to Type 2 Type 1 Hypervisors have direct access to hardware resources! Type 2 Hypervisors need to request resources from the OS first, the OS then accesses the hardware resources Hyper-V is Type 1
Hyper-V is a Type 1 Hypervisor! Can be confusing because on Windows 10 / 11 it's a Feature that's enabled from the Control Panel Can be confusing because on Server 2016/2019/2022 it's enabled as a Server Role Hyper-V Manager "appears" to look like an application, but this is what an administrator uses to create/manage VMs Hyper-V is the Virtual Machine Manager When Creating New VM’s When creating New Server VM’s use datacenter not standard. Datacenter supports clusters. For exporting and importing VMs from your home computer to the ICT Lab environment create a private vSwitch named "Private Virtual Switch" vSwitch names The name of the vSwitch is case sensitive. Your computer with Hyper-V already has the "Default Switch" configured To complete a successful Export (Copy/Backup) of a VM using Hyper-V Manager: Ensure the VM is shut down / turned off Remove the DVD / CD Drive from the VM Export the VM to the desired location using Hyper-V Manager by clicking Export ... (ie to an External Hard Drive - SSD) There are 3 Types of Imports when using Hyper-V Manager This type of import allows you to import, or "register," a VM where the files and VHD of the VM are already moved to the host You can perform this import when the files are already moved to the new host (ie VM files are cut and pasted from an SSD to a host computer prior to starting the Import process) This import will maintain the same unique ID this if faster then restore since it doesn't need to move a bunch of files. less work for hyper-v. This type of import allows you to import by copying the files and VHD of the VM are from one location to another This import will copy the VM files to a new host, the original files will remain in-tact on the original source (ie VM files saved on an SSD) The original exported files remain unchanged and can be reused for future imports This import will also maintain the same unique ID of the VM This type of import allows you to create "templates" of VMs This type of import can create multiple instances of the same VM on the same host This import will create a new ID for each VM You will not need to use this type of import for this course!

Cybersecurity analysts must prepare for any type of attack. It is their job to secure the assets of the organization’s network. Data is the one asset that cannot be replaced, it is the hardest to put a price on. To do this, cybersecurity analysts must first identify: Assets - Anything of value to an organization that must be protected including servers, infrastructure devices, end devices, and the greatest asset, data. Vulnerabilities - A weakness in a system or its design that could be exploited by a threat actor. Threats - Any potential danger to an asset. • The collection of all the devices and information owned or managed by an organization are assets. • The assets constitute the attack surface that threat actors could target. • As an organization grows, so do its assets. Consider the number of assets a large organization would have to protect. • Asset management consists of inventorying all assets, and then developing and implementing policies and procedures to protect them. • Organizations need to identify where critical information assets are stored, and how access is gained to that information.• Asset classification assigns an organization’s resources into groups based on common characteristics. • The most critical information needs to receive the highest level of protection and may even require special handling. • A labeling system can be used to determine how valuable, how sensitive, and how critical the information is. • The steps for identifying and classifying assets are: Determine the proper asset identification category: Information assets Software assets Physical assets Services Establish asset accountability by identifying the owner of each information asset and each piece of software: Identify the owner for all information assets. Identify the owner for all application software. Determine the criteria for classification Confidentiality Value Time Access rights Destruction Implement a classification schema: Adopt a consistent way of identifying information to ensure uniform protection and easier monitoring. Asset standards identify specific hardware and software products used by an organization. When a failure occurs, prompt action helps to maintain both access and security. If an organization does not standardize its hardware selection, personnel may need to scramble to find a replacement component. Non-standard environments require more expertise to manage, and they increase the cost of maintenance contracts and inventory • Part of the cybersecurity specialists’ job is to manage information assets and related systems throughout that asset´s lifecycle. The stages of asset´s lifecycle are: Procurement - The organization purchases the assets based on the needs identified from data gathered to justify the purchase. The asset is added to the organization’s inventory. Deployment -The asset is assembled and inspected to check for defects or other problems. Staff perform tests and install tags or barcodes for tracking purposes. The asset moves from inventory to in-use. Utilization -This is the longest stage of the cycle. The asset’s performance is continuously checked. Upgrades, patch fixes, new license purchases, and compliance audits are all part of the utilization stage. Maintenance It helps to extend an asset’s productive life. Staff may modify or upgrade the asset. Disposal - At the end of the asset’s productive life, it must be disposed of. All data must be wiped from the asset. Disposal may include dismantling an asset for parts. Any parts that can cause an environmental hazard must be disposed of according to local guidelines. have multiple layers of security to get to the asset eg AAA firewall IPS (intrusion prevention system) Hardened devices content filtering this is the key idea
the idea is that a threat actor will try to attack individual leaves to get to the data/core asset. To make sure data and infrastructure remain secure, an organization should create different layers of protection: Layering: To make sure data and information remains available, an organization must set up different layers of protection, creating a barrier of multiple defenses that work together to prevent attacks. Limiting: Limiting access to data and information reduces the possibility of a security threat. An organization should restrict access so that each user only has the level of access required to do their job. Diversity: If all defense layers were the same, it would not be very difficult for cybercriminals to succeed in an attack. The layers must be different so that if one layer is penetrated, the same technique will not work on all the others which would compromise the whole system Obscurity: Obscuring information can also protect data and information. An organization should not reveal any information that cybercriminals can use to identify which Operating System (OS) a server is running, or the type or make of equipment or software it uses. Simplicity: Complexity does not necessarily guarantee security. If employees do not understand how to configure a solution properly, such as setting up their account using an unnecessarily complex process, this may make it just as easy for cybercriminals to compromise those systems. • They are the guidelines that are developed by an organization to govern its actions. • The policies define standards of correct behavior for the business and its employees. • If behavior that violates business policy (baseline) is detected on the network, it is possible that a security breach has occurred. There are two types of Hypervisor: Type 1 and Type 2 Also known as the "Bare Metal Hypervisor" Type 1 Hypervisor is installed directly on the physical host Has direct access to the physical resources of the physical host which then allocates the available resources to the virtual machines Hypervisor loads (boots) first, before the Operating System Administrators have the ability to create clusters with many Type 1 Hypervisors (but not all) Also known as "Hosted Hypervisor" Type 2 Hypervisor is installed on top of the host Operating System (ie Windows 10) The host Operating System manages the hardware resources The Type 2 Hypervisor requests the resources from the Operating System Type 2 Hypervisors do not support clustering Type 1 Hypervisors have better performance compared to Type 2 Type 1 Hypervisors have direct access to hardware resources! Type 2 Hypervisors need to request resources from the OS first, the OS then accesses the hardware resources Hyper-V is Type 1

Hyper-V is a Type 1 Hypervisor! Can be confusing because on Windows 10 / 11 it's a Feature that's enabled from the Control Panel Can be confusing because on Server 2016/2019/2022 it's enabled as a Server Role Hyper-V Manager "appears" to look like an application, but this is what an administrator uses to create/manage VMs Hyper-V is the Virtual Machine Manager
